body: Actually I created the type `Hit` so I can reuse it here 👍
I don't necessarily need the "as string" but `getPropertyBypath` doesn't ensure the return type. It gives any type given by the path that resolved in the object. That's why I explicitly casted it.
Why do we do this? To copy the value or something else?
I'm still not convinced of writing the return type here, it can easily be inferred from the fact that .replace is called on escape (which always returns a string)

In the `snippet` (and `highlight`) Hogan helper, you don't pass the `hit` because you don't have access to it and we can infer it. Therefore the options that you pass are the snippet options, without the hit.

We explained it here: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/3617#discussion_r269201029.

Let's chat about it IRL if you're not convinced or need more details.
Good point – will remove this default value.
My question was about the JSON.parse, but I just realised that this was in the hogan helper
One of the purposes of the types is to reduce the cognitive overhead that reading code might produce. It's also about the contract, with the type definition the intent of the function is clearer.
would make sense to add HighlightResult as a type and then write all three possibilities with the result as an end factor
Thanks! I fixed that in d551209ae664e717685ef7d43150d83c716f679c for both highlight and snippet.

When it's not fully highlighted, the key is not returned:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6137112/55795602-856d4280-5ac8-11e9-8bce-75bbb005819f.png)

When it is fully highlighted, the attribute is `true`:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6137112/55795642-94ec8b80-5ac8-11e9-9434-2a7331cbe113.png)
wouldn't in that case the type be `fullyHighlighted?: true`? Although I guess technically it could still be false, and best to leave that case open
